title: plugin-09: Multi-region proof + config integration
summary: Secondo provider built-in, integrazione con keybinding/RPC e discovery delle actions.
description:
A second built-in provider, integrated with keybindings/RPC and action discovery — the multi-region proof.

═══ WHAT THIS PHASE ACTUALLY PROVES ═══

Everything in F003 is designed so that a component nobody special-cased behaves exactly like the
workspaces dock. **A second provider is the only way to find out.** Until one exists, every "any
component can do this" claim in the design is untested, and the shape of the first component leaks
into the host without anyone noticing — which has already happened repeatedly and each time was
found by building the general thing, not by reading.

Known, written-down places where the host is still workspaces-shaped (they are what this phase will
hit first):

- **`ChromeSignals` is workspace-keyed.** Every family but `row_nav` is keyed by `PaneId` / `ws_idx`
  / `col_idx`, so a second dock has nowhere to register a value that updates without a rebuild.
  `row_nav` shows the shape the rest wants: keyed by `(mount, nav_key)`, which any component can
  name.
- **`DragItemRegistry` is workspace-shaped** for the same reason: `ChromeDragItem` is a closed
  `Pane | Column | Workspace`, so a second dock's row cannot be dragged or dropped at all.

Both are recorded in `heca/src/chrome/contribution.rs` beside `BuildCx`, checked against "is this
true for ANY component?" on 2026-07-30 (F003/P086/T367).

═══ WHAT THE SECOND PROVIDER MUST GET FOR FREE ═══

If any of these needs a line written for the new component specifically, the host is the bug:

- rows with a keyboard cursor (`nav_key`), a right-click menu (`.context_menu`), and a `prefix+/`
  pick (`KeyHint::on_peek`) — none of which involves a registry;
- its own actions declared with `ActionMeta` (label, icon, declared `args`, policy, confirm), then
  reachable from a keybinding, the command palette and RPC with nothing further;
- **its own seating**: mounted twice, its two placements answer independently — the cursor, the
  scroll offset, the keyboard target and the gesture a row emits are all per mount
  (F004/P084/T399).

This is the same rule the whole feature rests on (`AGENTS.md` ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO): write the line a
plugin author would type; if it needs a registry, an id or a `pub(crate)` type, the API is the bug.

Design record: `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` §2.8 (chrome-wide, not sidebar-only), §3.2 (region
contributions), §3.4 (the provider model) · F003's description.
